Thanks — below is a 12-week, gym-based strength program tailored for a 36-year-old recreational lifter with a right medial meniscus repair/tear cleared for low-impact strength work only (no jumping, no deep knee flexion under load). The program prioritizes progressive strength, knee-friendly loading, neuromuscular control, and gradual reintroduction of ski-specific movements without impact. Before starting, confirm with the client’s surgeon/physio that all listed movements are safe for his specific repair/status, and progress only with pain-free range and no swelling increase.

Program structure and principles
- Frequency: 3 strength sessions per week (non-consecutive: e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri). Optional 1–2 low-intensity conditioning/recovery sessions per week (bike, pool, elliptical, walking). Avoid running/jumping until cleared.
- Phases: 4-week Hypertrophy/Foundational Strength (weeks 1–4), 4-week Strength & Stability (weeks 5–8), 4-week Intensification & Ski-specific Preparation (weeks 9–12).
- Progression: Increase load 2.5–5% when target reps can be completed with sound technique and no increased symptoms. Where absolute deep knee flexion is contraindicated, use partial range, tempo changes, or alternative exercises that load posterior chain and quad without deep flexion.
- Knee-safety rules: avoid loaded squats >~90° if instructed; avoid deep lunges or heavy step-downs >90°. Emphasize eccentric control, single-leg stability within safe ROM, and glute/hamstring strength to offload the knee.
- Warm-up: 8–12 min per session — light cardio (bike/elliptical), dynamic mobility (hip swings, ankle circles), and 2 warm-up sets for main compound lifts.
- Recovery and monitoring: track pain (0–10) and swelling each day. If pain increases >2 points or swelling appears, reduce load/volume and refer back to clinician.

Weekly layout (every week)
- Session A (Heavy lower-body emphasis + posterior chain)
- Session B (Upper body push/pull + core)
- Session C (Quad-focused but knee-safe + single-leg stability + conditioning)

Weeks 1–4: Foundational/hypertrophy (3x week) — objective: restore baseline strength, muscular balance, movement control; moderate load/higher volume; avoid deep knee flexion under load.
Session A
1. Warm-up: 8–12 min bike + hip mobility
2. Trap-bar deadlift (or hex-bar) — 4 sets x 6–8 reps — focus on moderate-heavy load; deadlift variation reduces knee shear relative to back squat. Avoid heavy single-leg deadlifts if balance compromises knee.
3. Split-stance Romanian deadlift (rear foot elevated RDL? keep small hip hinge) — 3 x 8 per leg (use DB or light barbell). Keep knee soft, hinge at hips; limit forward knee translation.
4. Glute bridge or barbell hip thrust — 4 x 8–12 — load heavy enough to challenge but no painful knee flexion.
5. Seated/lying hamstring curl — 3 x 10–12
6. Farmer carry or suitcase carry — 3 x 40–60s — builds core/bracing and control.
7. Core: Pallof press — 3 x 10/side

Session B
1. Warm-up: 8–12 min row/elliptical + shoulder mobility
2. Bench press (barbell or DB) — 4 x 6–8
3. One-arm DB row or chest-supported row — 4 x 8–10 per arm
4. Overhead press (standing or seated as tolerated) — 3 x 6–8
5. Lat pulldown or pull-up progression — 3 x 8–10
6. Face pulls — 3 x 12–15
7. Core: dead bug or anti-extension holds (ab wheel progressions if no lumbar pain) — 3 x 8–12

Session C
1. Warm-up: 8–12 min bike + single-leg balance drills (eyes open)
2. Bulgarian split squat to box (rear foot elevated or front foot on floor) — 4 x 6–8 per leg, box height set so front knee does not go past ~90° and ROM is comfortable. Keep loads moderate.
3. Step-ups to low box (50–60% body height) — 3 x 8 per leg (focus on controlled tempo); limit step height to avoid deep knee flexion.
4. Leg press — 3 x 10–12 with shallow–mid ROM (0–60–70° knee flexion), keep feet higher on plate to bias hips/glutes and protect knee.

Below is a practical, clinic-aware recovery and mobility plan tailored for your 36‑year‑old client recovering from a right medial meniscus tear (surgically cleared for low‑impact strength only). It’s designed to support the 12‑week strength + challenging low‑impact cardio program, reduce swelling, speed recovery, preserve knee health, and improve movement patterns relevant to skiing. Use pain and swelling as your primary guides — nothing should cause sharp knee pain or prolonged post‑session swelling. If swelling or pain rises, regress or consult his surgeon/physio.

Overview — goals and daily approach
- Daily micro‑dose mobility and activation (10–15 minutes) to reinforce movement patterns, reduce stiffness, and protect the meniscus.
- Post‑workout recovery routine (10–20 minutes) to expedite tissue recovery and reduce soreness.
- Weekly recovery sessions (1–2x/week) that include soft tissue work, low‑intensity movement, and targeted mobility.
- Sleep, nutrition, hydration, and simple therapeutic modalities to promote systemic recovery.
- Monitoring: daily knee check (pain 0–10 and visible swelling), readiness score (0–10), resting HR/training HR trends.

Daily knee check (before training)
- Pain: 0–10 scale. Proceed if pain ≤2 and does not increase after warm-up.
- Swelling: visible effusion or stiffness? If present or worsened, reduce load, substitute pool or upper-body session, or consult clinician.
- Readiness: subjective score 1–10. If ≤5, reduce volume or convert to technique/mobility session.

Warm-up mobility & activation (6–12 minutes before each session)
- Low-impact cardio 4–6 min (bike or elliptical) at easy pace to increase blood flow.
- Glute activation circuit (banded; 1–2 rounds, 8–12 reps each):
  - Banded lateral walks (mini‑band) — 10 steps each direction
  - Banded glute bridge or single‑leg bridge (double-leg if knee sensitive) — 10–12 reps
  - Banded clamshells — 10–12 reps each side
  - Banded monster walks (forward/back) — 8–10 steps
- Dynamic mobility (1 round):
  - Hip circles / hip CARs (controlled articular rotations) — 5 each way per side
  - Leg swings (front-to-back and side-to-side) — 8–10 each direction per leg (pain-free)
  - Ankle dorsiflexion mobilization (banded or wall) — 8–10 reps each side
  - Bodyweight shallow squat to box or 1/4–1/2 rep squat (no deep flexion) — 6–8 reps focusing on hip hinge and neutral spine

Post-workout recovery routine (10–20 minutes)
- Immediate cool-down: 5–8 minutes easy pedaling or walking to shuttle metabolites.
- Targeted mobility & soft-tissue (10–12 minutes):
  - Foam rolling (or soft tissue) 1–2 min each area: quads (light), hamstrings, glutes/IT band (glute med focus), calves. Avoid aggressive rolling directly on surgical scar; be gentle near knee.
  - Banded knee decompression / knee traction (if comfortable): Anchor band above knee and perform slow flexion/extension within pain-free ROM for 1–2 minutes to encourage synovial fluid movement (only if recommended by physio).
  - Hip flexor / quad stretch (kneeling lunge stretch, but keep knee on foam if sensitive) — 2 x 30s each side
  - Standing hamstring stretch or hamstring flossing — 2 x 20s each leg
  - Glute stretch (figure‑4 supine or seated) — 2 x 30s each side
  - Ankle mobility and calf stretch (standing) — 2 x 30s each side
- Contrast or cold (as indicated):
  - If knee swelling increases after sessions, apply ice 10–15 min (avoid prolonged icing). For non‑acute soreness, contrast showers or 10 min cold / 5 min heat can help. Use clinician guidance for modalities.

Weekly recovery sessions (1–2x/week; 20–45 minutes)
Option A — Mobility & prehab (25–35 minutes)
- Light aerobic warm-up: 6–8 min bike or pool
- Thoracic mobility: foam roll thoracic spine 2 min then T-spine rotations 2 x 8 each side
- Hip mobility flow (2 rounds):
  - 90/90 hip switches — 8 each side
  - Banded lateral hip distractions (1–2 min total each side)
  - Pigeon or half-pigeon modification if hip tolerates — 30s each side
- Knee-friendly quad/hip strength & control:
  - Short‑range Bulgarian or split squat isometric holds (box height no deep knee flexion) — 3 x 20–30s per leg
  - Banded monster walks + stepbacks — 2 x 12–15
- Core stability & anti-rotation:
  - Pallof press 3 x 8–10 each side
  - Dead bug 3 x 8–10
- Finish with 5–8 minutes of light mobility and breathing work

Option B — Aquatic recovery (if pool available; great if knee flares)
- 20–30 min pool session: easy laps or water walking, focusing on full ROM hip/knee movement without weight. Include:
  - 10 min continuous water walking (forward/backward, side shuffle)
  - 8 x 20–30m easy water sprints if tolerated
  - 5–8 min gentle dynamic stretching in shallow water

Prehab/strength maintenance for knee (3 x week short sessions, 8–12 minutes)
- Single-leg balance progression:
  - Single-leg stand 45–60s — eyes open → eyes closed progression
  - Progress to perturbations (ball toss, trainer nudges)
- Low-load eccentric control for step downs:
  - 3 x 6 slow step-downs from low box (eccentric 3–4s) each leg — pain-free
- Glute med & posterior chain mini circuit:
  - Side-lying clamshell 2 x 12–15
  - Single-leg Romanian hip hinge (DB) 2 x 8–10 per leg
  - Monster band walks 2 x 12 each way

Mobility drills for skiing posture and performance (3–4x/week, 6–10 minutes)
- 1. Deep hip hinge with reach (to train hip-dominant positions): 2 x 8–10 slow reps
- 2. Lateral lunge to half-turn (no deep knee flexion): 2 x 8 per side focusing on hip movement and core control
- 3. Loaded or unloaded ski stance holds (isometric) — slight flexion (~40–60°) for 3 x 30–45s; use light band for resistance if tolerable
- 4. Cable woodchop slow control: 2 x 8–10 per side to integrate rotational strength for skiing

Soft-tissue and manual therapy recommendations
- Weekly or biweekly sessions as needed: soft tissue work on quads/glutes/hamstrings and manual therapy for thoracic/hip restrictions can accelerate progress and reduce compensations.
- Use lacrosse ball for glute med release (1–2 minutes each side) and calf soft tissue as needed.
- Avoid aggressive deep work directly on the knee or scar without clinician approval.

Sleep, nutrition and systemic recovery
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours nightly; prioritize consistent bedtime routine. Use naps (20–30 min) on very heavy days if needed.
- Nutrition: maintain maintenance calories with protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg; distribute carbs around training to support high-volume weeks.
- Hydration & electrolytes: keep hydrated; consider small sodium intake if training heavy sweat sessions.
- Supplements (optional): creatine 3–5 g/day (supports recovery), omega‑3 (1–2 g EPA+DHA), vitamin D if low. Check with clinician.

Tools and modalities to consider (clinic-approved options)
- Compression sleeve or light compression wrap post-workout if mild swelling occurs.
- Cold packs for 10–15 min after sessions if swelling increases; contrast bathing for more general soreness.
- Percussive therapy (Theragun style) on muscles, avoiding direct knee joint or scar tissue — 30–90s per muscle group.
- Slideboard or skiErg as low-impact skill work that also aids recovery by maintaining neuromuscular patterning.

Monitoring and decision rules (when to regress)
- If knee pain increases >2 points on 0–10 scale or swelling appears:
  - Stop the offending drill.
  - Reduce strength volume by 25–50% and convert cardio to pool or easy bike for 72–96 hours.
  - Reintroduce loading gradually, starting with isometrics and light ROM movements.
  - Contact physio/surgeon if persistent pain or swelling >48 hours.
- If global recovery markers decline (resting HR up >8–10 bpm, sleep poor, appetite low, mood down), reduce weekly volume by 10–25% and emphasize sleep, nutrition, and one extra passive recovery day.

Goals: reduce total sets, push heavier loads, maintain control and single-leg work.

Session A
- Trap-bar deadlift: 5 × 3–5 (top sets ~85–90% of recent 5RM)

- Single-leg RDL: 3 × 5–6/leg
- Hip thrust: 4 × 5–6 (heavy)

Session B
- Bench/incline: 5 × 4–5
- Row: 4 × 5–6
- Overhead press: 3 × 4–6

- Cardio 1: 30–35 min tempo bike (2 × 8 min moderately hard).
- Cardio 2: HIIT 20–25 min (8 × 30s all-out / 90s easy).

Goals: neural strength, heavy triples/doubles; preserve form and knee safety.

Session A
- Trap-bar deadlift: 5 × 3 (work up to a heavy triple; target ~90–93% 1RM or heavy triple)
- Barbell RDL: 3 × 5 (heavy, controlled)
- Single-leg RDL: 3 × 4–5/leg
- Hip thrust: 4 × 4–6 (heavy)

Session B
- Bench press: 5 × 3 (heavy)

Session C

Goals: express maximal strength via doubles/singles with ample rest; keep knee healthy.

Session A
- Trap-bar deadlift: 4–5 × 2–3 (work up to heavy doubles or singles if technique perfect)
- Barbell RDL: 3 × 4–5 (lighter than deadlifts)
- Hip thrust: 3 × 3–4 (heavy)
- Single-leg RDL: 2–3 × 4/leg
- Sled pushes: 3 × 20–30 m (sharp)

Session B
- Bench: 4 × 2–3 (heavy)
- Heavy row/pull-up: 3 × 3–4
- Overhead press: 3 × 3
- Core: heavy anti-rotation 3 × 5–6/side

Session C
- Reverse Bulgarian: 3–4 × 4/leg
- Low box step-downs: 3 × 5/leg
- Unilateral leg press: 3 × 5–6
- Cable chops: 3 × 5–6/side

Cardio
- Cardio 1: 20–25 min tempo or short slideboard technique session (15 min)
- Cardio 2: Very short HIIT 10–15 min (6 × 20s all-out / long easy rest) — keep short volume

Week 12 — Peak / Taper (fresh, strong, ski-ready)
Goals: feel powerful, confident, and minimally fatigued. Test heavy single/double only if cleared and confident (prefer only one tested lift). Otherwise perform heavy but conservative top sets.

Session A (Mon) — Main heavy day
- Warm-up thoroughly.
- Trap-bar deadlift: work up to a heavy single/double OR heavy triple at ~90% (3–4 top sets total). Keep reps low (1–3).
- Hip thrust: 3 × 3–4 (moderately heavy)
- Hamstring curls or single-leg RDL: 2 × 5–6/leg
- Light sled: 3 × 20–30 m
- Finish: mobility + breathing

Session B (Wed) — Upper heavy but short
- Bench press: 3–4 × 2–3 (heavy)
- Row/pull-up: 3 × 3–5
- Overhead press: 2–3 × 3–4
- Core: light anti-rotation 2 × 6/side

Session C (Fri) — Activation / movement quality
- Reverse Bulgarian: 3 × 4–5/leg (lighter, focus on speed and control)
- Eccentric step-downs: 2 × 5/leg (clean)
- Sled push / prowler: 3 × 20 m (sharp)
- Single-leg balance + mobility: 10–15 min

Cardio (Week 12)
- Cardio 1: 15–20 min slideboard or tempo bike focusing on crisp technique
- Cardio 2: Optional 10–15 min light intervals or pool swim
- Prioritize rest; keep cardio short and specific

Peaking load guidelines (if 1RM unknown)
- Week 9: top sets ≈ 85–90% training max
- Week 10: top sets ≈ 90–93% for triples/doubles
- Week 11: top sets ≈ 92–95% for doubles/singles (only if technique perfect)
- Week 12: top sets ≈ 90% or heavy singles if testing — otherwise stay conservative

Cardio sessions — two per week (challenging, varied, low-impact)
Two weekly templates to rotate across the program; modality choices: bike, SkiErg, rower, slideboard, prowler/sled, elliptical, pool. Use the higher-intensity mixed-modal and sled + single-leg sessions described below, scaling rounds and rest per phase.

Cardio Session Template 1 — Mixed-Modal Intervals (30–35 min; challenging)
- Warm-up 6–8 min easy.
- Main: choose pattern for the week:
  - A) 8 rounds 40s work / 80s easy (alternate bike / SkiErg / row / slideboard each round)
  - B) 10 rounds 30s all-out / 30s easy (high intensity)
  - C) 4 rounds 4 min high tempo / 2 min easy (use bike or SkiErg)
- Cool-down 5–8 min + mobility.

Cardio Session Template 2 — Sled + Single-leg Circuit (25–40 min)
- Warm-up 6–8 min easy + hip activation
- Circuit (3–5 rounds; 60–90s rest between rounds):
  - Sled push heavy: 30s–40s or 20–40m
  - Single-leg pedal drill on bike: 60s/leg at moderate resistance
  - SkiErg or row: 60s high power
  - Slideboard carving: 45–60s tempo
- Cool-down + single-leg balance.

Progression across phases
- Weeks 1–3: lower intervals / shorter HIIT, more steady-state.
- Weeks 4–8: increase rounds, duration, or sled load for cardio; add mixed-modal challenges.
- Weeks 9–11: reduce cardio volume, keep intensity short and sharp.
- Week 12: short, technique-focused cardio sessions only.

Recovery & Mobility Plan (integrated)
Goals: manage swelling/pain, accelerate recovery, maintain mobility for skiing. Daily check: pain 0–10 and swelling. If pain >2 or swelling increases, reduce load and consult clinician.

Daily (5–15 min) — prehab & activation
- Easy 4–6 min bike to warm.
- Banded glute circuit: lateral walks 10 steps each way, clamshells 10–12/side, banded bridge 10–12.
- Leg swings 8–10 each direction per leg, ankle mobilizations 8–10 each side.
- 1–2 single-leg balance drills x 45–60 s (progress eyes closed).

Post-workout (10–20 min)
- Cool-down: 5–8 min easy pedal.
- Foam rolling: 1–2 min per muscle group (quads, hamstrings, glutes, calves) — be gentle near the knee and scar.
- Hip flexor stretch kneeling 2 × 30 s each side (use padding).
- Glute stretch figure‑4 2 × 30 s each side.
- Banded knee traction / movement (if physio approves) 1–2 min.
- If swelling: ice 10–15 min, elevate, compress as advised.

Weekly recovery sessions (1–2×)
Option A — Mobility & Prehab (25–35 min)
- T‑spine foam roll + rotations, 90/90 hip switches, banded lateral hip distractions, pigeon/horizontal hip mobility, short-range isometric Bulgarian holds 3 × 20–30 s/leg, Pallof presses 3 × 8–10, dead bug 3 × 10.

Option B — Aquatic recovery (20–30 min)
- Pool walking, water-based drills, easy water sprints as tolerated, gentle dynamic stretching in water.

Short prehab sessions (3×/week; 8–12 min)
- Single-leg balance & perturbations, slow eccentric step-downs 3 × 6/leg from low box, monster band walks 2 × 12.

Ski-specific mobility (3–4×/week; 6–10 min)
- Hip hinge with reach 2 × 8–10, lateral lunge to half-turn 2 × 8/side, isometric ski-stance holds 3 × 30–45 s (light flexion), cable woodchops 2 × 8–10/side.

Soft-tissue / manual therapy
- Weekly or biweekly sessions as needed. Use lacrosse ball for glute med release (1–2 min), avoid deep knee scar work without clinician approval. Percussive devices OK on major muscle groups, not on the knee joint.

Recovery monitoring and decision rules
- Morning readiness: if score ≤5/10 or resting HR >8–10 bpm above baseline, reduce volume ~25% or convert to pool/mobility session.
- Knee pain increase >2/10 or swelling: stop offending movement, reduce loading by 25–50% for 72–96 hours, use ice and elevation, consult physio if persistent >48 hours.
- Weekly weigh-in: maintain calories; if losing or gaining >0.5–1.0 kg over two weeks, adjust calories ±150–300 kcal.

Nutrition & recovery highlights
- Maintain weight: start near 30–33 kcal/kg/day (adjust to actual weight/activity). Protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day. Fat ~0.8–1.1 g/kg/day. Fill remaining calories with carbs, more on heavy/high-volume days.
- Pre/post workout: carbs + 20–40 g protein within 60–90 min post workout.
- Supplements: creatine 3–5 g/day, omega‑3s 1–2 g EPA+DHA, vitamin D if deficient — check clinician.

Weekly sample (integrated) — example microcycle for a high-volume week (Week 7)
- Mon: Strength A (heavy posterior) + post-workout recovery
- Tue: Cardio 1 (45–50 min steady + surges) + evening mobility
- Wed: Strength B (upper) + soft tissue
- Thu: Active recovery (pool or mobility 25–35 min)
- Fri: Strength C (single-leg emphasis) + post-workout mobility
- Sat: Cardio 2 (30–40 min mixed-modal HIIT) + balance work
- Sun: Rest / light walk / mobility

Coaching & implementation notes
- Warm-up cues: keep neutral spine, hinge at hips, control knee travel (avoid forward knee collapse), load glutes first.
- Exercise regressions: if any exercise causes symptoms, regress ROM (shallower), substitute (e.g., RDL instead of back squat), reduce load, or use pool sessions.
- Progression cues: increase load 2.5–5% when all reps and sets are completed with good form and no symptom increase. For cardio, increase rounds, decrease rest, or increase sled load/cadence.
- Testing: if testing a 1RM in week 12, limit to one lift (prefer trap-bar deadlift or bench), ensure full warm-up, and stop if technique or knee feels off. Prefer heavy doubles/triples otherwise.

Extras available on request
- Printable week-by-week calendar (PDF or spreadsheet).
- Percentage-based loads for main lifts if you supply current 1RMs or 3–5RMs.
- Exercise videos / cueing notes for any movement or regressions for specific knee ROM.
- A simple daily readiness checklist for the client to use before sessions.

Final safety reminder
- This program assumes the surgeon has cleared him for low‑impact strength work. Every progression must be pain- and swelling‑free. If the knee reacts, revert to lower load or pool-based training and consult the treating clinician.

If you want the 12‑week program exported as a printable schedule (calendar with each day’s exact sets/reps and suggested rests/RPE) or converted to % of 1RM for each main lift, give me his bodyweight and current 1RM/5RM estimates and I’ll prepare it.

Below is the full 12‑week, gym-based strength program for your 36‑year‑old recreational lifter returning from a right medial meniscus tear (cleared for low‑impact strength only). It integrates all prior adjustments: three strength sessions/week, two challenging low‑impact cardio sessions/week, increased volume in weeks 4–8, a structured peak (weeks 9–12) culminating in a fresh, strong-feeling week 12, and a recovery & mobility plan. Remind him to check with his surgeon/physio before progressing movements or ROM beyond what was cleared, and to stop any exercise that causes sharp pain or increases swelling.

High-level structure and principles
- Frequency: Strength 3×/week (Mon/Wed/Fri recommended). Cardio 2×/week (Tue/Sat recommended). One active recovery/light day (Thu) and one full rest day (Sun).
- Phases:
  - Weeks 1–3: Foundational / Hypertrophy (build base)
  - Week 4: End of foundational — bump volume to prepare for higher-volume block
  - Weeks 5–8: High-volume Strength & Stability (progressive volume increases; single-leg/eccentric emphasis)
  - Week 9: Intensity transition (reduce volume, increase intensity)
  - Weeks 10–11: Peaking high-intensity (low volume, heavy loads)
  - Week 12: Peak/taper (low volume, heavy but fresh; test heavy single/double if desired)
- Knee safety rules (must follow): no jumping, no running, no deep loaded knee flexion beyond clinician guidance (keep squats/lunges <~90° if advised), monitor swelling/pain; favor trap-bar, RDLs, hip-thrusts, sleds, and single-leg control within safe ROM.
- Warm-up: 6–12 min before sessions (bike/elliptical + dynamic mobility + glute activation).
- Progression: Load increases when reps are completed with good form and no increased symptoms. Use RPE and knee checks to guide.

Weekly layout (template)
- Mon: Strength Session A — Lower emphasis (posterior chain heavy)
- Tue: Cardio Session 1 — challenging low‑impact (steady/tempo or intervals depending on phase)
- Wed: Strength Session B — Upper body (push/pull) + core
- Thu: Active recovery / mobility (pool or mobility session)
- Fri: Strength Session C — Quad-driven but knee-safe + single-leg stability + sled/quality work
- Sat: Cardio Session 2 — high-intensity mixed-modal or sled + single-leg circuits
- Sun: Rest or gentle pool walk / mobility

Key equipment used: trap-bar (or hex), barbell, dumbbells, leg press, sled/prowler, bike (with watt meter if available), rower, SkiErg, slideboard, cable machine, bands, glute-ham developer (GHD) if available.

Phase-by-phase week-by-week plan

Weeks 1–3 — Foundational / Hypertrophy (moderate volume; build movement quality)
Goals: restore baseline strength, glute/hamstring dominance, single-leg stability; master technique; keep knee-friendly ROM.

Session A — Lower / Posterior (Mon)
- Warm-up: 6–8 min bike + band glute activation + ankle mobility
- Trap-bar deadlift: 4 × 6–8
- Romanian deadlift (barbell or DB): 3 × 8
- Barbell hip thrust (or heavy glute bridge): 4 × 8–12
- Seated or lying hamstring curl: 3 × 10–12
- Farmer carry / suitcase carry: 3 × 40–60 s

Recovery & Mobility Plan (integrated)
Goals: manage swelling/pain, accelerate recovery, maintain mobility for skiing. Daily check: pain 0–10 and swelling. If pain >2 or swelling increases, reduce load and consult clinician.

Daily (5–15 min) — prehab & activation
- Easy 4–6 min bike to warm.
- Banded glute circuit: lateral walks 10 steps each way, clamshells 10–12/side, banded bridge 10–12.
- Leg swings 8–10 each direction per leg, ankle mobilizations 8–10 each side.
- 1–2 single-leg balance drills x 45–60 s (progress eyes closed).

Post-workout (10–20 min)
- Cool-down: 5–8 min easy pedal.
- Foam rolling: 1–2 min per muscle group (quads, hamstrings, glutes, calves) — be gentle near the knee and scar.
- Hip flexor stretch kneeling 2 × 30 s each side (use padding).
- Glute stretch figure‑4 2 × 30 s each side.
- Banded knee traction / movement (if physio approves) 1–2 min.
- If swelling: ice 10–15 min, elevate, compress as advised.

Weekly recovery sessions (1–2×)
Option A — Mobility & Prehab (25–35 min)
- T‑spine foam roll + rotations, 90/90 hip switches, banded lateral hip distractions, pigeon/horizontal hip mobility, short-range isometric Bulgarian holds 3 × 20–30 s/leg, Pallof presses 3 × 8–10, dead bug 3 × 10.

Option B — Aquatic recovery (20–30 min)
- Pool walking, water-based drills, easy water sprints as tolerated, gentle dynamic stretching in water.

Short prehab sessions (3×/week; 8–12 min)
- Single-leg balance & perturbations, slow eccentric step-downs 3 × 6/leg from low box, monster band walks 2 × 12.

Ski-specific mobility (3–4×/week; 6–10 min)
- Hip hinge with reach 2 × 8–10, lateral lunge to half-turn 2 × 8/side, isometric ski-stance holds 3 × 30–45 s (light flexion), cable woodchops 2 × 8–10/side.

Soft-tissue / manual therapy
- Weekly or biweekly sessions as needed. Use lacrosse ball for glute med release (1–2 min), avoid deep knee scar work without clinician approval. Percussive devices OK on major muscle groups, not on the knee joint.

Recovery monitoring and decision rules
- Morning readiness: if score ≤5/10 or resting HR >8–10 bpm above baseline, reduce volume ~25% or convert to pool/mobility session.
- Knee pain increase >2/10 or swelling: stop offending movement, reduce loading by 25–50% for 72–96 hours, use ice and elevation, consult physio if persistent >48 hours.
- Weekly weigh-in: maintain calories; if losing or gaining >0.5–1.0 kg over two weeks, adjust calories ±150–300 kcal.

Nutrition & recovery highlights
- Maintain weight: start near 30–33 kcal/kg/day (adjust to actual weight/activity). Protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day. Fat ~0.8–1.1 g/kg/day. Fill remaining calories with carbs, more on heavy/high-volume days.
- Pre/post workout: carbs + 20–40 g protein within 60–90 min post workout.
- Supplements: creatine 3–5 g/day, omega‑3s 1–2 g EPA+DHA, vitamin D if deficient — check clinician.

Coaching & implementation notes
- Warm-up cues: keep neutral spine, hinge at hips, control knee travel (avoid forward knee collapse), load glutes first.
- Exercise regressions: if any exercise causes symptoms, regress ROM (shallower), substitute (e.g., RDL instead of back squat), reduce load, or use pool sessions.
- Progression cues: increase load 2.5–5% when all reps and sets are completed with good form and no symptom increase. For cardio, increase rounds, decrease rest, or increase sled load/cadence.
- Testing: if testing a 1RM in week 12, limit to one lift (prefer trap-bar deadlift or bench), ensure full warm-up, and stop if technique or knee feels off. Prefer heavy doubles/triples otherwise.
